next_steps: Send Dedicated trial pricing and SLA options
Schedule POC scoping with infra (Devon) for week of 5/21
Share SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration notes
action_items: Maya Chen: Share tracing best-practices doc and demo recording — due 2028-05-16
Evan Patel: Run sample request-log export for Atlas test cluster and share results — due 2028-05-21

summary: AE + SE walked Atlas Health through the Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs workflows. Main topics: correlating traces to request IDs, filtering logs for high-latency tokens, and debugging a failing private deployment path. Agreed next steps include sharing security docs, exporting request logs for a sample failure, and scheduling a POC scoping session.
transcript:
Header: 2028-05-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Evan Patel, Lina Gomez, Devon Carter, Priya Singh

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, Maya Chen from Redwood, thanks for joining. We've got Evan on the call too, he'll drive the console walkthrough.
00:10 Evan: Hi all, Evan Patel, SE. Quick agenda: tracing overview, error analysis, request logs, and then a short debugging demo for a failing private deployment. Any additions?
00:22 Lina: That works. We're most interested in tracing -> request log correlation, and how to quickly find failing prompts in a PII-sensitive environment.
00:30 Maya: Perfect, we'll call out the RBAC/SOC2 pieces as we go.
01:05 Evan: Opening the console now, so you can see the Traces page. We group by request id, and spans show model calls, routing, cache hits — sometimes the auto-transcription prints K-V cache as K V cache, so apologies if the UI label seems off.
02:15 Devon: Quick question: can we filter traces by customer tenant id? We have a multi-tenant VPC setup.
02:31 Evan: Yes, you can scope by tenant tag at the top-level filter. We also have attribute filters — region, model variant, and commit id. For private deployments the tenant tag flows from the control plane but you can also inject custom metadata.
03:10 Priya: For audit, does the trace contain user-level PII? We need to ensure logs are redacted or removed.
03:28 Maya: Good point. By default request payloads are not persisted in plaintext in the long-term tracing view; we have redaction flags and retention policies. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS notes after the call.
04:05 Evan: Back to the timeline — here you can click a trace and expand spans. See this long span — it's a model fallback. That correlates to a routing decision, which links to the request-log entry.
04:52 Lina: The fallback here, is that the dedicated to hosted failover? How frequent do those happen?
05:06 Evan: It depends on capacity and policy. You can set fallback to a cheaper variant or different region. We log the reason code in the trace so you can filter for fallback events.
06:00 Evan: Now switching to Error Analysis. This view groups by error signature and shows top failing prompts. Note the transcribed prompt examples are fuzzy — sometimes punctuation is off, and proper nouns get mangled (e.g. KV cache spelled as K V cache).
06:45 Devon: Is there an ability to export the top failing prompts for offline analysis?
06:55 Evan: Yes, export CSV or JSON for a given time window and error signature. We also attach request IDs so you can pull the full request-log for replay.
07:40 Lina: If we have encrypted payloads in transit, can we still trace end-to-end? The concern is we can't send raw prompts to Redwood.
07:56 Maya: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSMs; we can also enable local redaction before the trace is indexed. Evan will note the exact options in the doc.
09:15 Evan: Showing request logs now — this is the raw request-log table. You can search by request id, model, status code, latency. Use the quick filters to show high-latency requests (> 500ms) or error codes 5xx.
10:02 Lina: How granular are the timestamps? We need token-level timing to see where latency spikes.
10:18 Evan: We capture per-span timing but token-level timing is available when you enable the debug trace mode or when you run a token-profiler on a dedicated node. Token timing can be noisy; we provide smoothed aggregates in the console.
11:05 Devon: For our internal monitoring we prefer exporting logs to our ELK. Do you have a streaming export?
11:20 Evan: Yep, we support Kafka and S3 export hooks and also a direct push to common logging endpoints. For Private, you can run the export inside your VPC so data never leaves.
12:10 Priya: About RBAC — can we make the request logs visible to infra but hide prompts from support?
12:26 Maya: Yes, RBAC is attribute-based; you can grant view-only request metadata without payloads. We map Redwood roles to your SAML groups during SSO setup.
13:00 Evan: Next I'll show a debugging flow: here's a failing trace that correlates to a 502 from the model stack. You can see in the spans that the model process crashed after a large prompt.
13:40 Lina: Can we replay that request to a sandbox to reproduce?
13:52 Evan: We provide a replay button that pushes the request to an isolated sandbox model variant — it strips any customer secrets if redaction is enabled. If you want a full raw replay we'll need explicit controls enabled in your environment.
15:10 Devon: Our main blocker is we saw intermittent timeouts when we route through our private gateway to Redwood. Could be MTU or TLS handshake issues. Does the console surface TLS handshake failures?
15:30 Evan: We surface connection-level errors in the request logs with error codes; we also annotate traces with network layer failures when detected. For TLS we'd show the handshake failure in the earliest span.
16:05 Maya: On the pricing/ops side, note that high token counts and debug traces increase ingestion and storage; for POC we recommend sampling or enabling debug tracing only for a percentage of requests. That keeps costs predictable.
17:00 Lina: What's the usual guidance for sampling?
17:10 Evan: Start with 1% debug sampling for production traffic and 100% for canaries. You can bump sampling for a particular route or user ID as needed.
18:20 Priya: We need to confirm data residency — some of our PHI must remain in EU region. Can you pin traces and logs to a region?
18:38 Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported in both Hosted and Private modes; for Private you control the storage endpoint. We'll attach the endpoint mapping in the follow-up doc.
19:22 Evan: Back in the Error Analysis UI, click into a signature — we show stack snippets, example prompts, and suggested remediation (e.g., reduce context length, switch to quantized model). These are suggestions based on our heuristics.
20:05 Lina: Those suggestions look useful. Do you support automated rollouts based on those signals?
20:20 Evan: You can wire the console alerts to a webhook that triggers a rollback or traffic-shift policy in the deployment layer — we have canary and A/B rollout integrations.
21:00 Devon: For the POC we'll probably start on Dedicated GPU pool, to keep latency tighter. How do we compare Dedicated vs Hosted for tail latency?
21:20 Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower variance in queuing latency. Hosted can be cheaper at scale but has more variance during peak. We provided a benchmarking spreadsheet in the sales folder — I'll re-share it.
22:10 Evan: Demo: here's a request that hit a large tail latency due to cache miss — trace shows 'prefix cache miss' and long decode span. You can click 'suggest fix' to see the batching/quantization recommendation.
23:05 Lina: Does that suggestion include switching quantization like 4-bit Q4 or is that automatic?
23:20 Evan: It's a recommendation only; actual quantization is applied at model onboarding and must be validated. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles per workload.
24:00 Priya: About compliance: do you store audit logs for who accessed traces? We need 7 years for some regs.
24:14 Maya: Audit logs (access events) can be forwarded to your SIEM and we retain them per contract — we can extend retention for enterprise.
25:00 Evan: Now demonstrating request-log export — filter to errors in the last 24h, export JSON — the file includes request ids and trace links. I'll trigger an export.
25:45 Evan: Export complete. I'll attach the export to the follow-up and also run a sample that filters by the failing request IDs you send.
27:00 Lina: We're concerned about prompt leakage in support tickets when we escalate. Is there an on/off toggle to hide prompts from Redwood support?
27:18 Maya: Yes — you can set support access to "metadata-only" and enable a support escalation flow that requires customer approval to include raw prompts. We'll document the exact flow.
28:10 Devon: For private deployment debugging, what level of visibility do your SEs need in our VPC? We want minimal access.
28:30 Evan: Typically we request a temporary bastion or logs export to a secure S3 bucket. We also support a read-only role that surfaces metrics without exposing payloads.
29:05 Lina: Can we attach our own correlation IDs from our front-end so trace <-> request matches our telemetry?
29:20 Evan: Absolutely, pass X-Correlation-ID and it becomes a primary index in the trace view.
30:10 Priya: We have an existing alerting system — can Redwood emit alerts for error-rate increases?
30:24 Evan: Yes, console supports alert rules and can push to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhooks.
31:00 Maya: Quick note on costs: debug traces and full request logs are charged differently; we'll put expected ranges in the pricing sheet.
31:35 Lina: Ok. Would like to do a short POC: 2-week Dedicated trial with sampling and a focused set of routes.
31:52 Maya: Sounds good. We'll put a POC proposal in the follow-up — sample size, success metrics, and commit/CPE.
33:05 Evan: Now a short troubleshooting demo — reproducing a 502 by replaying the request to an isolated dev model. Watch the trace: model process OOMs at the decode step.
33:45 Devon: OOM on decode suggests large context; can we limit max tokens per request server-side?
33:58 Evan: Yes, there's a hard limit per route and a soft limit with warnings. We can enforce both.
35:10 Priya: If we enforce token caps, can clients get a structured error so UX can handle gracefully?
35:25 Evan: Yes, we return a structured JSON error with code and suggested action, which shows up in the Error Analysis UI.
36:10 Lina: For POC acceptance criteria, we'll want <100ms median and <300ms 95th for key routes, and errors <0.5%.
36:28 Maya: Noted. We'll bake that into the POC doc and include instrumentation instructions so you can validate metrics from your side.
37:15 Evan: Final quick tip: use trace sampling on canaries at 100% and production at 1-2%, and set a rule to escalate if canary error rate > threshold.
38:00 Lina: Thanks — that was very helpful.
38:10 Maya: Recap: Maya will share pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, and the demo recording; Evan will run the request-log export for the sample cluster; Atlas will provide failing request IDs and acceptance criteria.
38:35 Devon: I'll coordinate infra availability for the POC week of 5/21.
38:50 Priya: We'll send over the SAML group mapping for RBAC next week.
39:10 Maya: Any other questions?
39:20 Lina: None from me.
39:25 Evan: Great, thanks everyone.
39:30 End of recording.
